# Open Cube OS Interface Reference (3.0.0-WP04)

Every entry below is extracted from the real tree at generation
time: the L0 command declarations straight from the OC_SHELL_CMD
call sites, the ring-3 surface from the ush SVC_CMDS table and
src/L0/services/sysapi/l1svc_defs.h, the kernel-side declarations from the
service headers. Regenerate with `make api-docs`.

- v1.0.0 commands (compatibility baseline): **233** - all mapped
  below, none dropped
- 3.0.0-WP04 command homes: **285 total** = 0 in the L0 recovery
  shell + 0 ring-3 SYS_L1SVC ops + 11 ush built-ins
- L1SVC service surface: **20 categories / 190 numbered ops**
- Kernel-side declarations across the service headers: **76**
- Syscalls: 54 (`grep -c '#define SYS_' src/L0/services/sysapi/core_syscall.h`,
  SYS_L1SVC(110) added in 2.0.0)
- Source lines: **128,890** across 624 files (README verification
  command; .c/.h/.S, generated data blobs excluded)

2.0.0 is a breaking re-architecture, stated precisely (2.1.0
correction of the over-general 2.0.0 phrasing): the three
driver-family register hooks (`driver_block_register`,
`driver_nic_register`, `driver_snd_register`) moved from the
public v1 L1 headers into the per-family internal headers
(`services/*/drv_internal.h`, 'internal since 2.0.0'); drivers
and services now declare their identity in-file via
OC_DRIVER_DECL / OC_SERVICE_DECL; every operational command
class moved to the ring-3 service surface; and the only true
deletions on the v1 numbered surface are the two entries in the
deletion register (Part 2d). Other register-class declarations
(tui_ext.h menus/pages/widgets/..., `watchdog_register`,
`signal_register`, `shell_register_builtin`) are STILL PUBLIC
in the v2 tree - the per-entry truth is Part 2c. What
deliberately stays in L0: the kernel self-tests, the watchdog,
the crash policy controls, the kernel log readers
(dmesg/logcat/logctl/crashlog/dumpinfo/crashtest), the chipset
diagnostics, the recovery-environment file commands, and the
interactive session commands (ssh/sshd).

### 1b - Ring-3 service commands (ush, 0 SVC rows + 11 built-ins)

The default boot entry (ush, ring 3) routes these through
SYS_L1SVC(110) to the owning L0 service; the built-ins run
entirely in ring 3 (classic file/process syscalls) or through
the SYS_NETCMD bridge ().

## Part 1c - v1.0.0 -> 3.0.0-WP04 command mapping (233 rows)

The compatibility contract: every 1.0.0 command and where it
lives now. `L0` = recovery shell (same name), `SVC` = ring-3
service surface (same body, captured output), `builtin` = ush
built-in, `bridge` = ush built-in reaching the L0 body through
SYS_NETCMD, `L0-only` = recovery-environment command kept out

selects the services/`<category>`/ folder, op selects the command.
Renumber only by appending (see src/L0/services/sysapi/l1svc_defs.h).

## Part 2c - v1.0.0 -> 3.0.0-WP04 interface-surface comparison (278 entries)

2.1.0 (P-04): the per-entry truth behind 'the register class
is gone'. The v1 README formula counted 162 numbered L1
extension interfaces; the v1 Part 2 tables are the complete
unfiltered declaration truth of the 13 L1 surface headers -
**278 callable rows** - and this comparison covers every one
of them (a superset of any numbered subset; the 2.0.0
postcheck's 163-row parse was itself incomplete and missed
three of the deletions below). Their fate in the current
tree: **251 public + 0 internalized + 27 gone = 278.**

## Part 2d - Deletion register (declared, complete)

Every v1.0.0 surface-header declaration with NO counterpart
anywhere in the current tree - the complete declared deletion
list. There are exactly **27**; nothing else on the v1
surface was removed (the remaining 251 entries are public or
internalized per Part 2c). All deletions are *init/probe
plumbing*, not user-visible capability: the functionality
was rebuilt inside the v2 service model - each row names
where.

| v1 entry | v1 header | What it did | Why removed | Rebuilt where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `void driver_block_init(void);` | `drivers/block/driver_block_blk.h` | hardcoded per-driver block-layer init walk | v2 drivers self-register via OC_DRIVER_DECL and services self-initialize from the collected OC_SERVICE_DECL linker sections - a hardcoded walk contradicts the model | `block_svc_init()` in `services/block/block_svc.c` (OC_SERVICE_DECL_L1 in `services/block/block_l1.c`) |
| `int driver_nic_init(void);` | `drivers/nic/driver_nic.h` | hardcoded per-family NIC init walk | same self-declaration model | `nic_svc_init()` in `services/nic/nic_svc.c` (`services/nic/nic_svc.h`) |
| `int driver_nic_probe_all(void);` | `drivers/nic/driver_nic.h` | hardcoded probe list over all NIC families | the probe list is COLLECTED from per-driver OC_DRIVER_DECL identities instead of hardcoded | `nic_svc_probe_all()` in `services/nic/nic_svc.c` (`services/nic/nic_svc.h`) |
| `void driver_snd_init(void);` | `drivers/snd/driver_snd.h` | hardcoded sound-driver init walk | same self-declaration model | `snd_svc_init()` in `services/snd/snd_svc.c` (`services/snd/snd_svc.h`) |
| `int driver_snd_probe_all(void);` | `drivers/snd/driver_snd.h` | hardcoded probe list over all sound drivers | same collection model (see `services/snd/snd_svc.c`) | `snd_svc_probe_all()` in `services/snd/snd_svc.c` (OC_SERVICE_DECL_L1 late probe, `services/snd/snd_l1.c`) |

'Register class gone' - the exact statement (2.1.0
correction):

- The register-class hooks of the three driver families
  were NOT deleted - they moved from the public v1 L1 headers
  into the per-family internal headers 'internal since
  2.0.0' (`driver_block_register` AND the block family's
  `driver_block_register_device` / `_unregister_device` /
  `driver_block_set_ops` -> `services/block/drv_internal.h`;
  `driver_nic_register` -> `services/nic/drv_internal.h`;
  `driver_snd_register` -> `services/snd/drv_internal.h` -
  6 entries in Part 2c marked internalized). They are
  driver-private plumbing now, not an L1 extension surface.
- Still-public register-class declarations in the current
  tree: the `tui_*_register` families (`tui/tui_ext.h`),
  `watchdog_register` (`services/watchdog/core_watchdog.h`),
  `signal_register` (`services/l1/l1_wp8a.h`),
  `shell_register_builtin` (`services/l1/l1_wp8cd.h`) and
  `l1_ext_shell_register_command_ex`
  (`services/l1/l1_ext.h`).
- The only true deletions on the v1 surface are the 27 rows
  above.

## Part 3 - Syscall surface (54)

Defined in `src/L0/services/sysapi/core_syscall.h` (`#define SYS_*`).
ABI: rax = number, rdi/rsi/rdx/r10 = arguments (r8 = 5th for
SYS_L1SVC), rax = result (>= 0 success, < 0 error).
SYS_L1SVC(110) and SYS_NETCMD(101) are the 2.0.0 ring-3
service bridges.
